items.title_orig: Jamison Wake Trades Religion For Rock
items.article_text:
Jason and Paul welcome Jamison Wake to the show to discuss his life as a pastor turned rocker. After nearly two decades as a Christian minister, Jamison Wake traded the pulpit for the stage. On his new album, The Wheel, he explores fatherhood, masculinity, faith, American life, and personal reinvention through cinematic, anthemic rock. We talk about leaving the ministry, rediscovering his musical roots, confronting disillusionment, and finding new ways to build community through music.

items.title_orig: Eddie Vedder and Stephen Wilson Jr. release stunning version of Temple Of The Dog's Hunger Strike
items.article_text:
Hunger Strike was filmed live during Steven Wilson Jr.'s set at Ohana Fest in California last month

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Last month, Eddie Vedder and Friends headlined the opening night of Vedder's Ohana Fest in Dana Point, California, but the Pearl Jam frontman returned to the festival the following night to guest with country and rock singer-songwriter Stephen Wilson Jr.

Much to the delight of those lucky enough to be in attendance, Vedder sidled onto the stage during Wilson Jr.'s set to share vocals on a stunning version of Hunger Strike, the classic Temple Of The Dog single originally fronted by Vedder and late Soundgarden singer Chris Cornell. The collaboration has now been officially released on pro-shot video.

"Thank you, Temple Of The Dog!" exclaims Wilson Jr. at the song's climax. "What the hell just happened?"

Instigated by Cornell, Temple Of The Dog were formed to pay tribute to late Mother Love Bone frontman Andrew Wood by recording two songs Cornell had written in 1990 after the death of his former roommate.

After hooking up with Mother Love Bone guitarist Stone Gossard and bassist Jeff Ament, plus Mike McCready, the guitarist from their fledgling new band Pearl Jam, and Soundgarden drummer Matt Cameron, the proposed single swiftly became a full album.

Hunger Strike, the album's standout, was only written because Cornell didn’t like that the number of songs the band originally wrote – nine – was odd. And so a classic was born.

Wilson Jr. is currently on tour in Europe, having completed a British and Irish tour at the weekend. He's scheduled to play a run of US dates in November and December, ending with a show at the Choctaw Casino & Resort in Durant, OK., on New Year's Eve. Full dates below.
